audit.whatIsWrong: Abscond / Abduct is described as 'his dash + stun (recast pull)' in three fields.
audit.why: Riot's text gives it a dash and a recast chain-pull and no crowd control at all. The already-audited sylas__warwick mirror removed the same false stun claim from its side.
audit.corrected: Named as a dash plus recast pull with no stun, and given its real 13s rank-1 cooldown as the commit window.
sources: Sylas kit E text and cd 13/12/11/10/9

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike said Infinite Duress pins him, and never named what Hijack actually does in this specific matchup.
audit.why: Hijack steals Warwick's own ultimate on an 80s rank-1 cooldown — the shortest ult cooldown in the lane — so a Warwick who leaps first hands Sylas a 1.5s suppression to use back on him.
audit.corrected: Spike rewritten around baiting the stolen ult before committing, with Hijack's 80s cooldown stated.
sources: Sylas kit R text and cd 80/55/30

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl appeared nowhere in the lane text.
audit.why: It is the ability that most reliably breaks a counted Sylas all-in: 2.5s of damage reduction and then a 1-second fear, on 15s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Written into the mid text with its duration structure and cooldown; Kingslayer's healing tied to Grievous Wounds in the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers agree with each other and with the packet chart (Warwick-favoured), but the already-audited sylas__warwick mirror flipped rows 1-5 to Sylas and row 6 to Skill.
audit.why: The two charts are opposites and Warwick's 53.53% over 1246 games supports this side, so I did not flip rows on a guess.
Spike stages are right — level 3 Blood Hunt, level 6, first item, and the isolated late 1v1 — and level 6 now carries the Hijack ordering rule.

edits.before: His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His dash and its recast pull — there is no stun. Bait it, then commit in the 13s window.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct (13s at rank 1): matchup-defining — a dash and recast pull, no stun. Bait it, then commit. - Kingslayer heals him off you: Grievous Wounds before you all-in. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Sylas's Abscond / Abduct: His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. When it is down — Q-bite, E-fear, out-sustain.
edits.after: Track Abscond / Abduct (13s): a dash plus recast pull, no stun. When it is down — Q-bite, Primal Howl his commit, out-sustain.

edits.before: W Blood Hunt speed lets you dodge his E2 Abscond/Abduct chain-pull and Q Chain Lash, then Q Jaws in — his lifesteal-heal off you means you must trade when his Q is on cooldown.
edits.after: Blood Hunt speed lets you dodge Abduct's chain-pull and Chain Lash (Q), then Q-bite in — Kingslayer (W) heals him off you, so trade while his Q sits on its 10s cooldown.

edits.before: R Infinite Duress pins Sylas so he can't Abscond dash away, but if he steals your ult (or a better one) the fight shifts — bait his stolen R before you commit yours.
edits.after: Hijack (R) steals Infinite Duress itself and is 80s at rank 1 — bait the stolen ult out first and only then leap, or you eat your own 1.5s suppression.

edits.before: Levels 3-4 are yours with Blood Hunt speed to dodge his E chain and punish, and Q sustain to shrug his poke. Level 5 is Skill as his combo comes online, but you flip Level 6 by pinning him through his dash with R before he can Abscond.
edits.after: Levels 3-4 are yours with Blood Hunt speed to dodge his chain and punish, and Q sustain to shrug his poke. Level 5 is Skill as his combo lands, and at 6 hold Primal Howl (15s) for his all-in — 2.5s of damage reduction, then a fear, breaks it mid-combo.

notes: Same false claim the mirror found on its side was live here too: Abscond / Abduct was written as a stun in three fields; Riot's text gives it no CC. Highest-value addition is Hijack's 80s rank-1 cooldown and the fact that what he steals is Infinite Duress itself. Level chart left untouched: both layers already agree and match the packet chart and the 53.53% win rate, while the mirror recorded the opposite — flagged rather than guessed.
